summary: Verifies and attests that books, art, music, photos and video were made by humans (or discloses how AI was used), working for publishers, newsrooms, labels, galleries, contests and certification bodies such as the Authors Guild's Human Authored program, using provenance standards like C2PA Content Credentials alongside process evidence and interviews. AI helps most with organizing evidence dossiers, interpreting provenance manifests, drafting consistent criteria and reports, and tracking fast-moving disclosure rules like EU AI Act Article 50, while the certifier keeps the judgment and the signature.

prompts.title: Evidence dossier triage
prompts.task: Organize a creator's submitted process evidence and find gaps before review
prompts.prompt: You are assisting an authenticity certifier who attests that creative work is human-made. Below is the evidence a creator submitted for [WORK TITLE, MEDIUM]: [LIST OF EVIDENCE: drafts with timestamps, version history, layered source files, raw camera files, session recordings, tool list, signed declaration]. Our certification criteria are: [PASTE CRITERIA, including what AI assistance is permitted, e.g. spellcheck allowed, generative drafting not]. Produce: (1) a table mapping each criterion to the supporting evidence and its strength (strong/moderate/weak/none); (2) gaps or inconsistencies, such as timeline jumps or missing intermediate versions; (3) specific follow-up requests to send the creator. Do not render a verdict; flag anything you cannot assess from descriptions alone.
prompts.caution: Absence of evidence is not proof of AI use; the certifier makes the determination and the creator should get a chance to respond.

prompts.title: Read a C2PA manifest
prompts.task: Interpret Content Credentials output in plain language
prompts.prompt: I am reviewing a file's C2PA Content Credentials as part of a human-made media certification. Here is the output from [TOOL, e.g. c2patool or the Content Authenticity Initiative Verify site]: [PASTE MANIFEST JSON OR SUMMARY]. Explain in plain language: the claim generator and signer, the chain of ingredients and actions (e.g. c2pa.created, c2pa.edited, any digitalSourceType such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia), whether the signature and hard binding validated, and what the manifest does NOT prove. Then list what would make me suspicious (stripped or re-signed manifests, untrusted certificates, mismatched timestamps). Format as short sections plus a checklist. Say where you are unsure of a field's meaning under C2PA spec version [VERSION].
prompts.caution: C2PA proves what a signer asserted and that the file was not altered since, not that the assertion is true; missing credentials are common and not evidence of AI.

prompts.title: Write certification criteria
prompts.task: Draft a tiered human-made standard for a new medium
prompts.prompt: Help me draft certification criteria for human-made [MEDIUM, e.g. illustration, music recordings, documentary photography] for [ORGANIZATION TYPE]. Define tiers such as 'fully human-made', 'human-made with disclosed AI assistance', and 'not eligible', with concrete examples of permitted and prohibited tool uses in this medium (e.g. noise reduction, auto-tune, generative fill, AI stem separation). For each tier specify required evidence, how it is verified, and how disclosures should be worded. Compare with existing approaches, such as the Authors Guild Human Authored certification, Content Credentials digitalSourceType values, and the US Copyright Office's 2025 guidance on human authorship, and flag where the field has no consensus. Output as a draft policy document with open questions at the end.
prompts.caution: Check every cited program's current terms directly; these programs and definitions are changing quickly.

prompts.title: Detector result interpretation
prompts.task: Weigh AI-detection tool scores without overrelying on them
prompts.prompt: An AI-text or AI-image detector ([TOOL NAME]) gave [WORK] a score of [SCORE] for being AI-generated. Context: [CREATOR BACKGROUND, e.g. non-native English writer, heavy stylistic editing, genre]. Explain what this kind of detector measures, its known false-positive and false-negative patterns (including documented bias against non-native writers and against heavily edited or compressed images), and how much weight it deserves next to process evidence like [OTHER EVIDENCE]. Recommend how to record it in my review file and what further verification would be proportionate. Be explicit about uncertainty, and do not treat the score as dispositive.
prompts.caution: Never deny or revoke certification on a detector score alone; documented false positives harm real creators.

prompts.title: Certification report
prompts.task: Draft the formal attestation report for a reviewed work
prompts.prompt: Draft a certification report for [WORK TITLE] by [CREATOR] under [STANDARD NAME AND VERSION]. My findings: [YOUR NOTES: evidence reviewed, interviews, provenance results, any disclosed AI assistance, decision]. Structure: scope of what was certified (exact files, versions, hashes [HASHES]); method; evidence summary; disclosed tool use; determination and tier; limitations (what certification does not guarantee); validity period and revocation conditions. Use precise, non-promotional language and avoid claiming more certainty than the evidence supports. Mark any sentence where my notes are thin with [CERTIFIER TO CONFIRM].
prompts.caution: The signed determination is the certifier's; keep the report scoped to the exact files reviewed.

prompts.title: Dispute and appeal response
prompts.task: Respond to a creator contesting a denial or a third party challenging a certified work
prompts.prompt: I need to respond to [A CREATOR APPEALING A DENIAL / A THIRD PARTY ALLEGING A CERTIFIED WORK USED AI]. Their message: [PASTE]. Our original findings: [SUMMARY]. Our appeals policy: [PASTE OR DESCRIBE]. Draft (1) an internal memo listing which claims are new evidence versus disagreement, what to re-examine, and whether to suspend the label during review; (2) a respectful, factual reply that explains next steps and timelines without disclosing other parties' confidential material or speculating about intent. Keep the reply under [WORD LIMIT] words. Flag any legal exposure (defamation, contract terms) for counsel review.
prompts.caution: Public accusations about a named creator carry defamation risk; route anything public through legal.

prompts.title: Regulatory watch brief
prompts.task: Track disclosure and labeling rules affecting clients
prompts.prompt: Prepare a briefing on AI-content disclosure and provenance rules relevant to [CLIENT TYPE, e.g. a book publisher selling in the EU and US / a stock photo agency]. Cover, as applicable: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations and the Commission's code of practice on marking AI-generated content, California's AI Transparency Act (SB 942) and later amendments, platform labeling policies of [PLATFORMS], and C2PA adoption by [CAMERA MAKERS, PLATFORMS]. For each: what it requires, who it binds, effective date, and how a human-made certification interacts with it. Output a table plus a 'what changed recently / what to verify' list. My knowledge date is [DATE]; clearly mark anything that may be outdated or that you are not sure exists.
prompts.caution: Verify dates and obligations against the official texts; implementation dates have shifted and guidance is still being issued.

prompts.title: Upskilling plan
prompts.task: Build a learning plan for the technical and forensic side of the job
prompts.prompt: I am an authenticity certifier with a background in [BACKGROUND, e.g. editorial / art history / photojournalism] and I want stronger technical skills. Build a [N]-week study plan covering: how generative image, audio and text models work at a conceptual level; C2PA and JPEG Trust (ISO/IEC 21617) provenance concepts and hands-on use of c2patool; basic media forensics (EXIF, error level analysis, compression artifacts, audio spectrograms) and their limits; digital signatures and certificate trust; and interviewing creators about their process. For each week give goals, a hands-on exercise on my own sample files, and the kind of primary source to read (specs, NIST or academic papers). Note which skills are evolving fastest.
prompts.caution: Forensic heuristics age quickly as models improve; treat any single technique as one signal among several.
